body: I cannot reproduce this, so installation _does_ matter. (Honestly, the template is there for a reason!)

@clason 

Really no matter.

```
$ mkdir ~/test
$ cd ~/test
$ wget https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/nightly/nvim.appimage
$ chmod u+x ./nvim.appimage
$ ./nvim.appimage --clean
:function foobar
```
Cannot reproduce either, tested on both nightly and the nvim Appimage on lxterminal. Maybe something specific to Kali Linux?
Tested on latest kali docker image, couldn't reproduce there either :/.
The only specific thing is that function name cannot start with a small letter (this is why `E128` is expected). The latest build on Win11 crashes as well.
Yes, but I get exactly the described expected behavior with your example. So something must be wrong with your build, and we need to figure out what.

Okay, this is l10n bug. Occurs only with Russian locale.

```
:let $LANG="ru"
:func foobar
```

> Okay, this is l10n bug. Occurs only with Russian locale.
> 
> ```
> :let $LANG="ru"
> :func foobar
> ```

Can't reproduce with this either. There's more going on.
I can reproduce this after adding `ru_RU.UTF-8 UTF-8` to `/etc/locale.gen` and running `sudo locale-gen`, then running `LC_ALL=ru_RU.UTF-8 nvim --clean`.

stab in the dark, but can you try removing this line: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0a81a33a9d0fe6c61ab98da0c0212b3b343f3591/src/nvim/po/ru.po#L962
and rebuilding?

@clason 
Yes, it works. Just run `msgfmt ru.po` and moved the resulting file where it belongs. It appears as all fixed.

That causes the error message to contain two `%s`, while only one additional argument is passed to `semsg()`, which causes `str_arg` to be an invalid value at the second `%s` here:
<https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0a81a33a9d0fe6c61ab98da0c0212b3b343f3591/src/nvim/strings.c#L982-L983>

> @clason
> Yes, it works. Just run `msgfmt ru.po` and moved the resulting file where it belongs. It appears as all fixed.

Want to make a PR?

(I didn't see this line in another translation, so it's likely spurious.)
Okay, I'll do it. Have to read through it at first though. I see at least one more message (E883) was truncated.
If there are other problems you can fix at the same time, go for it!
